citation.authors: Oh H, Lincoln K, Waldman K

cited_by.title: Colourism, skin tone and mental health

record.population: Black American adults, National Survey of American Life 2001-2003 (probability sample)
record.finding: In-group colourism (from other Black people) was associated with greater odds of any lifetime psychiatric disorder (aOR 1.20, 95% CI 1.08 to 1.32); out-group colourism was not (aOR 1.08, 0.99 to 1.18). In-group colourism was linked to alcohol use, substance use, anxiety and eating disorders, but not PTSD or mood disorder. The authors say more research is needed to understand why.
record.note: Association from one survey, perceived colourism self-reported; not a trial and not proof of cause.
